newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain mkts to shrug off data, focus on EMU - MSI.
newsitem.headline: Spain mkts to shrug off data, focus on EMU - MSI.

text.p: Spanish inflation might end 1997 higher than expected and economic growth below target, but Spain's likely entry into a single European currency from 1999 will continue to drive the country's financial markets, a Morgan Stanley International (MSI) report said.

The report, dated November 12, forecast average 1997 inflation at 2.9 percent, with a likely pickup in the second half. It also expected 1997 gross domestic product (GDP) would average 2.7 percent over the course of the year but may hit three percent year-on-year in the last quarter.

That compares with official forecasts for 3.0-percent real GDP growth in 1997 and Bank of Spain governor Luis Angel Rojo's inflation prediction at the end of 1997 between 2.5 and 2.6 percent. Rojo made his prediction before a senate committee early on Thursday.

MSI said the expected lower economic growth and a worse-than-expected trend in the ex-central government deficit will push the overall government deficit to overshoot the 3.0-percent of GDP target outlined in the Mastricht Treaty for European economic and monetary union (EMU), MSI said.
Nevertheless, the brokerage firm said it expected "the interest rate spread versus Germany to narrow further over the course of 1997, with the ten-year spread moving towards 100 basis points."

And a likely ratio of the overall deficit to GDP of around 3.6 percent in 1997 should not keep Spain out of EMU from its start because it would not necessarily be that far from France's ratio, which is forecast at 3.2 percent, MSI said.
Furthermore, "the government may well implement additional budget measures," it added.
